chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from one who heard Abu Sayyar say: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:

Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to Yusuf (peace be upon him) while he was in prison and said: Say after every obligatory prayer: 'O Allah, grant me relief and a way out, and provide for me from where I expect and from where I do not expect,' three times.

key_terms.دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ مَفْرُوضَةٍ: Dubur kulli salatin mafruda - after every obligatory prayer: a recommended time for supplication in Islamic practice
key_terms.فَرَجًا: Faraj - relief/deliverance: divine opening from distress, a key concept in Shia eschatology and personal supplication
key_terms.مَخْرَجًا: Makhraj - a way out: exit from difficulty, paired with faraj to cover both spiritual relief and practical escape

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Angel Gabriel teach Prophet Yusuf in prison according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Angel Gabriel (AS) visited Prophet Yusuf (AS) in prison and taught him a supplication to recite after every obligatory prayer, asking Allah for relief, deliverance, and sustenance from expected and unexpected sources. This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), connects the prophetic experience of Yusuf's imprisonment with a practical devotional act accessible to all believers facing hardship. The supplication emphasizes both divine relief (faraj) and provision (rizq), reflecting the Quranic account of Yusuf's eventual liberation.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Hammad b. `Uthman from one who heard Aba Sayyar say: I heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:

Gabriel (as) came to Yusuf (as) when he was in prison and said: “After every obligatory prayer, say: ‘O Allah! Grant me relief and deliverance and give me sustenance from where I expect and from where I do not expect (Allahummaj`al li farajan wa makhrajan warzuqni min haythu ahtasibu wa man haythu la ahtasib)’ three times.”
